Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.11 (definition of spt T, chapter-06.txt lines 297–301); the partition-of-unity argument below is the standard reason why the union in 2.11 is itself a set on which the current vanishes. Notation: "S vanishes on W" means S(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W.
1. K := tsupport ω is compact and K ⊆ U, because ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is a compactly supported smooth form with tsupport ω ⊆ U. If K = ∅ then ω = 0 and S(ω) = 0 by linearity; assume K ≠ ∅.
2. Since K ⊆ U and K ∩ spt S = ∅, we have K ⊆ U ∖ spt S ⊆ Z_S. By compactness there are finitely many open sets W₁,…,W_m from the family defining Z_S (each with S vanishing on W_i) such that K ⊆ W₁ ∪ … ∪ W_m.
3. Take a smooth partition of unity on ℝ^P subordinate to the open cover {W₁,…,W_m, ℝ^P ∖ K} (e.g. Mathlib's SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate for the closed set K and the cover by W₁,…,W_m): smooth ψ₁,…,ψ_m : ℝ^P → [0,1] with tsupport ψ_i ⊆ W_i for each i and Σ_i ψ_i(y) = 1 for every y ∈ K.
4. For each i, ψ_iω (pointwise product of a smooth function and a smooth n-form) is smooth, and tsupport(ψ_iω) ⊆ tsupport ψ_i ∩ tsupport ω ⊆ W_i ∩ K; in particular it is compact and contained in U. Thus ψ_iω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport(ψ_iω) ⊆ W_i, and S(ψ_iω) = 0 since S vanishes on W_i.
5. ω = Σ_i ψ_iω pointwise: if ω(y) ≠ 0 then y ∈ K and Σ_iψ_i(y) = 1; if ω(y) = 0 both sides vanish. By linearity of S, S(ω) = Σ_i S(ψ_iω) = 0.

Source: Part B (B1–B6) of the selected parent's supplied proof, i.e. Simon Ch. 6, 2.25 (homotopy formula for the affine homotopy h(t, x) = tx from f = 0 to g = id), 2.30 (the cone 0 ⨯ S := h_#([[(0,1)]] × S)), 2.31 (∂(0 ⨯ S) = S − 0 ⨯ ∂S) and 2.32 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 441–451 and 528–551). As in the supplied proof, h_#([[(0,1)]] × ·) is written at the level of forms through the Poincaré homotopy operator K. One specialization: the continuity step B4 uses the hypothesis S.mass ≠ ∞ (in the selected parent S is integer multiplicity with compact support, and its finite mass is delivered by the sibling im_parametrization) instead of the general C^m estimate of the supplied B4; only sup-norm bounds are then needed.

Notation and tools.
- k := n + 1 ≥ 1. For p ∈ ℕ, Λ^p := Covector (Euclid P) p (continuous alternating p-linear maps (ℝ^P)^p → ℝ) and 𝒟^p := TestFormOn univ p (C^∞ maps ℝ^P → Λ^p with compact support). For α ∈ Λ^p, ‖α‖ is the operator norm (Mathlib norm of ContinuousAlternatingMap) and |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α is the Euclidean coefficient norm (|α|_E² = Σ_I α(e_{I_1}, …, e_{I_p})² over strictly increasing I).
- d = exteriorDerivative = Mathlib extDeriv. At a point x where β is differentiable, dβ(x)(w_0, …, w_p) = Σ_{i=0}^p (−1)^i Dβ(x)[w_i](w_0, …, ŵ_i, …, w_p) (exteriorDerivative_apply / extDeriv_apply: ∑ i, (−1)^i • fderiv ℝ (fun y => β y (i.removeNth w)) x (w i)). In particular dβ(x) depends only on β on a neighbourhood of x.
- For p ≥ 1, α ∈ Λ^p and x ∈ ℝ^P, ι_xα := α.curryLeft x ∈ Λ^{p−1}, so ι_xα(v) = α(Fin.cons x v) =: α(x, v). The map (α, x) ↦ ι_xα is continuous bilinear and ‖ι_xα‖ ≤ ‖α‖‖x‖.
- spt X = X.support = univ ∖ Z_X, where the zero region Z_X is the union of the open W with compact closure on which X vanishes; Z_X is open (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion), so spt X is closed.
- Sibling support_vanishing (Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support): if X ∈ 𝒟_p(U), γ ∈ 𝒟^p(U) and tsupport γ is disjoint from spt X, then X(γ) = 0. Consequence (L), locality: if γ, γ' ∈ 𝒟^p agree on an open set V ⊇ spt X, then X(γ) = X(γ'). Indeed γ − γ' vanishes on V, so its support lies in the closed set ℝ^P ∖ V, hence tsupport(γ − γ') ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ V is disjoint from spt X; by support_vanishing and linearity X(γ) − X(γ') = X(γ − γ') = 0.
- Sibling param_integral (Submission.cmcdt_lpo_slice_param_integral): if V is a complete real normed space and h : ℝ × ℝ^P → V is C^∞, then x ↦ ∫_0^1 h(t, x) dt is C^∞, and its derivative at x is ∫_0^1 D_x h(t, x) dt (the integral of the partial derivatives fderiv ℝ (fun x' => h (t, x')) x).

Step 1 (the homotopy operator; B1). For p ≥ 1 and a C^∞ map β : ℝ^P → Λ^p put h_β(t, x) := t^{p−1} • ι_x(β(t • x)) ∈ Λ^{p−1} and (K_pβ)(x) := ∫_0^1 h_β(t, x) dt (interval integral in the finite-dimensional, hence complete, space Λ^{p−1}).
 (a) h_β is C^∞ on ℝ × ℝ^P: t ↦ t^{p−1} and (t, x) ↦ β(t • x) are C^∞ and (α, x) ↦ ι_xα is continuous bilinear. By param_integral, K_pβ is C^∞ and D(K_pβ)(x) = ∫_0^1 D_x h_β(t, x) dt for every x.
 (b) Evaluation at a fixed v ∈ (ℝ^P)^{p−1} is a continuous linear map Λ^{p−1} → ℝ and commutes with the interval integral, so (K_pβ)(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^{p−1} β(tx)(x, v) dt. By (a), the product rule for the bilinear ι and the chain rule D_x[β(tx)][w] = t·Dβ(tx)[w], for every w: D[y ↦ (K_pβ)(y)(v)](x)[w] = ∫_0^1 t^{p−1}[t·Dβ(tx)[w](x, v) + β(tx)(w, v)] dt.

Where only the integrability of a single term is needed, the supplied bound via A2a is replaced by the cruder operator-norm bound below, which uses the integrability hypothesis (iv).

Notation. k := n + 1, so ℝ^{k+1} = Euclid (n + 2). For z ∈ ℝ^{k+1} let s(z) := (WithLp.ofLp z) 0 ∈ ℝ and τ(z) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)) ∈ ℝ^k; ι(t, u) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp u)) is the inverse map ℝ × ℝ^k → ℝ^{k+1}. s and τ are continuous linear maps with |s(z)| ≤ ‖z‖, ‖τ(z)‖ ≤ ‖z‖, s(e_0) = 1, τ(e_0) = 0, s(e_{b+1}) = 0, τ(e_{b+1}) = e'_b, where e and e' are the standard bases of ℝ^{k+1} and ℝ^k. For vectors v_0, …, v_m let J(v) := (det[⟨v_a, v_b⟩]_{a,b})^{1/2}. For ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1} put ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_y ‖ω(y)‖ (operator norm; finite since ω is continuous with compact support). Let L_j be a Lipschitz constant of F_j.

Step 1 (Fubini on cylinders; F2). The map z ↦ (s(z), τ(z)) is a measurable linear equivalence ℝ^{k+1} → ℝ × ℝ^k that carries Lebesgue measure to the product of the Lebesgue measures (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp and MeasureTheory.volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove (fun _ => ℝ) 0). Hence, for Borel A ⊆ ℝ^k, the cylinder Cyl(A) := {z : s(z) ∈ (0, 1), τ(z) ∈ A} is Borel; ∫⁻_{Cyl(A)} f = ∫⁻_A ∫⁻_{(0,1)} f(ι(t, u)) dt du for every Borel f : ℝ^{k+1} → [0, ∞] (Tonelli); and ∫_{Cyl(A)} f = ∫_A ∫_{(0,1)} f(ι(t, u)) dt du for every real f integrable on Cyl(A) (Fubini). (These three facts are the comparator-accepted lemma cmcdt_lpi_cyl_fubini, which a decomposition of this node may reuse at its identical type.)

Step 2 (radius and retraction; F1). spt S is compact, so there is ρ > 0 with spt S ⊆ ball(0, ρ). Let r_ρ(y) := y if ‖y‖ ≤ ρ and r_ρ(y) := (ρ/‖y‖)y otherwise; r_ρ is the nearest-point projection onto the closed convex ball B̄ := closedBall(0, ρ), and it is 1-Lipschitz. Indeed, with p := r_ρ(x) one has ⟨x − p, z − p⟩ ≤ 0 for every z ∈ B̄ (if ‖x‖ ≤ ρ then x − p = 0; otherwise x − p = (1 − ρ/‖x‖)x and ⟨x, z⟩ ≤ ρ‖x‖ = ⟨x, p⟩). For q := r_ρ(y) this gives ⟨x − p, q − p⟩ ≤ 0 and ⟨y − q, p − q⟩ ≤ 0; adding, ‖p − q‖² ≤ ⟨x − y, p − q⟩ ≤ ‖x − y‖‖p − q‖, so ‖p − q‖ ≤ ‖x − y‖. Put F̂_j := r_ρ ∘ F_j: it is L_j-Lipschitz, ‖F̂_j‖ ≤ ρ, and F̂_j = F_j on the open set O_j := F_j⁻¹(ball(0, ρ)), which contains A_j by (vi).

Step 3 (definitions). Let σ(t) := min(max(t, 0), 1) (1-Lipschitz, values in [0, 1], σ(t) = t for t ∈ [0, 1]). Define G_j(z) := σ(s(z)) • F̂_j(τ(z)), B_j := Cyl(A_j) and w_j(z) := g_j(τ(z)).
 (a) B_j is Borel (Step 1) and w_j is measurable (g_j measurable, τ continuous).
 (b) G_j is Lipschitz: ‖G_j(z) − G_j(z')‖ ≤ |σ(s(z)) − σ(s(z'))|·‖F̂_j(τ(z))‖ + σ(s(z'))·‖F̂_j(τ(z)) − F̂_j(τ(z'))‖ ≤ ρ|s(z) − s(z')| + L_j‖τ(z) − τ(z')‖ ≤ (ρ + L_j)‖z − z'‖.
 (c) (w_j : ℝ) is integrable on B_j: by Step 1 (Tonelli), ∫⁻_{B_j} |w_j| = ∫⁻_{A_j} ∫⁻_{(0,1)} |g_j(u)| dt du = ∫⁻_{A_j} |g_j| < ∞ by (iv).

Step 4 (derivative on B_j; F3). Let z ∈ B_j, t := s(z) ∈ (0, 1), u := τ(z) ∈ A_j. The set {z' : s(z') ∈ (0, 1), τ(z') ∈ O_j} is an open neighbourhood of z on which G_j(z') = s(z') • F_j(τ(z')). F_j is differentiable at u by (v), and s, τ are linear, so by the product rule G_j is differentiable at z with DG_j(z)h = s(h)·F_j(u) + t·DF_j(u)(τ(h)). Hence DG_j(z)e_0 = F_j(u) and DG_j(z)e_{b+1} = t·DF_j(u)e'_b, i.e. ∂G_j(z) = Fin.cons (F_j u) (t • ∂F_j(u)).

Step 5 (integrand). For ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1} and z ∈ B_j (t, u as in Step 4), multilinearity in the last k arguments gives ω(G_j z)(∂G_j z) = ω(t • F_j u)(Fin.cons (F_j u) (t • ∂F_j u)) = t^k·ω(t • F_j u)(Fin.cons (F_j u) (∂F_j u)).

Step 6 (cone Jacobian; A4). Let a, w_1, …, w_k ∈ ℝ^P and t ≥ 0.
 (a) J(a, tw_1, …, tw_k) = t^k J(a, w_1, …, w_k): the Gram matrix of (a, tw) is D·Gram(a, w)·D with D := diag(1, t, …, t), so its determinant is t^{2k} det Gram(a, w).
 (b) J(a, w) ≤ ‖a‖·J(w). If w is linearly dependent, so is (a, w), and both Gram determinants vanish (Gram(v)c = 0 for a nonzero c with Σ c_a v_a = 0). Otherwise let π be the orthogonal projection onto W := span(w) and a' := a − πa = a − Σ_i c_i w_i. Replacing a by a' is the column operation Gram(a', w) = Eᵀ·Gram(a, w)·E with E unipotent (det E = 1), and since a' ⊥ W the matrix Gram(a', w) is block diagonal with blocks ‖a'‖² and Gram(w). Hence det Gram(a, w) = ‖a'‖²·det Gram(w) ≤ ‖a‖²·det Gram(w).
 Consequently, for z ∈ B_j (t, u as in Step 4), JG_j(z) = J(F_j u, t∂F_j u) = t^k J(F_j u, ∂F_j u) ≤ t^k‖F_j u‖·JF_j(u) ≤ ρ·JF_j(u), because 0 < t < 1 and ‖F_j u‖ < ρ by (vi).

Step 7 (total weight; F5). By Step 6, Step 1 (Tonelli) and (vii): Σ_j ∫⁻_{B_j} |w_j|·JG_j ≤ Σ_j ∫⁻_{A_j} ∫⁻_{(0,1)} |g_j(u)|·ρ·JF_j(u) dt du = ρ·Σ_j ∫⁻_{A_j} |g_j|·JF_j < ∞.

Step 8 (representation; F4). Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1} and take γ from (ix): R(ω) = S(γ) and γ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^k ω(tx)(Fin.cons x v) dt for x ∈ spt S. By (viii), HasSum (j ↦ I_j) (S(γ)) with I_j := ∫_{A_j} g_j(u)·γ(F_j u)(∂F_j u) du. Fix j and put Φ_j(z) := w_j(z)·ω(G_j z)(∂G_j z).
 (a) For u ∈ A_j, F_j(u) ∈ spt S by (vi), so by (ix) and Step 5 (at z = ι(t, u) ∈ B_j for t ∈ (0, 1); the interval integral over [0, 1] equals the integral over (0, 1)): g_j(u)·γ(F_j u)(∂F_j u) = ∫_0^1 g_j(u) t^k ω(tF_j u)(Fin.cons (F_j u) (∂F_j u)) dt = ∫_{(0,1)} Φ_j(ι(t, u)) dt.
 (b) Φ_j is integrable on B_j. It is measurable: w_j is measurable, G_j is continuous, z ↦ DG_j(z) is Borel (Mathlib measurable_fderiv), and (y, v) ↦ ω(y)(v) is continuous. For every z, ‖DG_j(z)‖ ≤ ρ + L_j (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz and Step 3(b)), so |Φ_j(z)| ≤ |w_j(z)|·‖ω‖_∞·∏_{a=0}^{k} ‖DG_j(z)e_a‖ ≤ (ρ + L_j)^{k+1}‖ω‖_∞·|w_j(z)|, which is integrable on B_j by Step 3(c).
 (c) By Step 1 (Fubini) and (a): ∫_{B_j} Φ_j = ∫_{A_j} ∫_{(0,1)} Φ_j(ι(t, u)) dt du = I_j.
 Hence HasSum (j ↦ ∫_{B_j} w_j(z)·ω(G_j z)(∂G_j z) dz) (S(γ)) = HasSum (…) (R(ω)).

Steps 3(a)–(c), 7 and 8 give the conclusion. ∎
proof_key_steps: Coordinates z = ι(s, u) on ℝ^{n+2} ≅ ℝ × ℝ^{n+1} carry Lebesgue measure to the product measure: Tonelli/Fubini on cylinders (0,1) × A.
Bound F_j by the 1-Lipschitz radial retraction onto B̄_ρ ⊇ spt S without changing it near A_j; G_j(z) := σ(s(z))·F̂_j(τ(z)) is Lipschitz, B_j := (0,1) × A_j, w_j := g_j∘τ is integrable on B_j.
On B_j, G_j = s·F_j(τ) near z, so ∂G_j = (F_j(u), t∂F_j(u)) and ω(G_j)(∂G_j) = t^{n+1} ω(tF_j u)(F_j u, ∂F_j u).
Cone Jacobian: J(a, tw) = t^{n+1}J(a, w) ≤ t^{n+1}|a|J(w), so JG_j ≤ ρ JF_j and Σ∫|w_j|JG_j ≤ ρΣ∫|g_j|JF_j < ∞.

Since F_j(A_j) ⊆ spt S, the cone formula and S's representation give R(ω) = S(γ) = Σ_j ∫_{A_j} g_j ∫_0^1 t^{n+1}ω(tF_j)(F_j, ∂F_j) dt du = Σ_j ∫_{B_j} w_j ω(G_j)(∂G_j) by Fubini (integrability from the operator-norm bound).

Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the density argument in the proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒” (chapter-03.txt lines 107–160); Ch. 6, Remarks 3.2(1) and 2.9 (chapter-06.txt lines 287–293, 755–768), stated in the book without proof; and Ch. 6, Remark 2.6 for the orientation bound. Hⁿ := μHE[n] throughout. For x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap). The statement has four parts: (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces, (b) restriction of a representation to a Borel set, (c) differences of integer multiplicity currents, (d) the orientation bound |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α|; U is open in (a)–(c).

Preliminaries.
(P0) Normalization: SimonGMT's density theorems are stated for simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n, which equals μHE[n] for natural n (SimonGMT Chapter02 simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, with simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure); hence null sets, finiteness and densities transfer verbatim, and Hⁿ is Borel regular (every set has a Borel hull of the same measure).
(P1) Scaling: for every set A, Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(A)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(A) (Mathlib Measure.hausdorffMeasure_smul₀ and invariance of Hausdorff measure under isometries). Hence for Borel A and bounded Borel f, ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} f dHⁿ = r^{−n}∫_A f(η_{x,r}(y)) dHⁿ(y).
(P2) Density zero (SimonGMT Chapter01 simon_theorem_3_6, for the Borel regular outer measure Hⁿ, cf. simon_remark_3_7_hausdorff): if D is Borel with Hⁿ(D) < ∞, then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ D, lim_{r↓0} Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x))/(ω_n rⁿ) = 0.
(P3) Cauchy–Binet. For n×P matrices A, B, det(ABᵀ) = Σ_I det(A_I) det(B_I), the sum over increasing I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n) in {1, …, P}, A_I the n×n submatrix of columns I. Proof: the j-th column of ABᵀ is Σ_k B_{jk}A_{·k}, so by multilinearity det(ABᵀ) = Σ_{k_1,…,k_n} B_{1k_1}⋯B_{nk_n} det(A_{·k_1}, …, A_{·k_n}); terms with a repeated index vanish, and grouping the remaining tuples by their underlying increasing tuple I (k = I ∘ σ for a permutation σ) gives Σ_I det(A_I) Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_j B_{j, I_{σ(j)}} = Σ_I det(A_I)det(B_I). (For n > P both sides are 0 — no increasing I, and rank ABᵀ < n.)
(P4) Orientation bound. If τ_1, …, τ_n are orthonormal in ℝ^P and ⟨α, ζ⟩ = ±α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors α, then |⟨α, ζ⟩| ≤ |α| (Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm). Proof: with A_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩, multilinearity and the alternating property give α(τ) = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_I); by Cauchy–Schwarz and (P3), |α(τ)| ≤ |α|(Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2} = |α| det(AAᵀ)^{1/2} = |α|, since AAᵀ = (⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) is the identity. For n = 0, |α(∅)| = |α|.
(P5) Two unit orientations of the same n-dimensional subspace Q differ by a sign: if τ, τ' are orthonormal bases of Q, τ'_i = Σ_j O_{ij}τ_j with O orthogonal, and α(τ') = det(O)α(τ) = ±α(τ) for every alternating α. Hence IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q and IsUnitOrientationOf ζ' Q imply ζ' = ζ or ζ' = −ζ, and IsUnitOrientationOf (−ζ) Q holds whenever IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q.
(P6) If R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in an open U, then Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (θ ≥ 1 on M).

(d) Orientation bound. By the orientation field of an IMRep, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier there is Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient x) Q, i.e. an orthonormal τ with ⟨α, R.orient x⟩ = ±α(τ) for all α; by (P4), |R.orient x α| ≤ |α| for all α. (No openness of U is needed.)

(a) Locality. Let U be open, M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and D := M' ∖ M.
1. For R ∈ ℕ let U_R := {x ∈ U : |x| < R, infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/R} (U_R := {|x| < R} if U = ℝ^P). U_R is open, closure(U_R) is a compact subset of U, and U_R ↑ U. D_R := D ∩ U_R is Borel with Hⁿ(D_R) ≤ Hⁿ(M' ∩ closure(U_R)) < ∞. By (P2) there is an Hⁿ-null set Z_R such that every x ∉ D_R ∪ Z_R satisfies Hⁿ(D_R ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ) as r ↓ 0. Let Z := ⋃_R Z_R, and let Z' ⊇ Z be a Borel Hⁿ-null set (P0). Let x ∈ M ∖ Z'; choose R with x ∈ U_R and r₀ > 0 with B̄_{r₀}(x) ⊆ U_R. Then x ∉ D_R (as x ∈ M) and D ∩ B̄_r(x) = D_R ∩ B̄_r(x) for r < r₀, so Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ).
2. Fix such x, a subspace Q and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_ρ(0). For r < r₀/ρ the sets η_{x,r}(M), η_{x,r}(M') meet B_ρ(0) in sets of finite Hⁿ-measure, so the integrals below are genuine Bochner integrals. Since η_{x,r} is injective, η_{x,r}(M') is the disjoint union of η_{x,r}(M) and η_{x,r}(D), and by (P1)
 |∫_{η_{x,r}(M')} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ| = |∫_{η_{x,r}(D)} f dHⁿ| ≤ |f|_∞ r^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ B_{rρ}(x)) → 0 as r ↓ 0.
